sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the name Yeshurun, implying a gift, seems to emphasize the equal essence of the soul more than the name Yaakov, which relates to inheritance.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
that the matter of the essence of the soul, from which perspective all Jews are equal,
is emphasized more
(seemingly)
in the name Yeshurun,
for Yeshurun is from the term “song” (shir) that has no beginning or end,
and nevertheless the name Yeshurun relates to the matter of a gift
(of the Torah)
which belongs to the will of the giver,
while regarding inheritance, which belongs to the bequeather himself, it is said “Morashah Kehilas Yaakov.”
And this will be understood by prefacing what is said,
“He will choose for us our inheritance, the pride of Yaakov, etc.,”
which mentions two matters here.
“He will choose for us” —
the matter of choice,
and “our inheritance” —
the matter of inheritance.
And it can be said,
that the matter of choice, that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose Israel, is that He chose to desire them.
And the matter of inheritance, that the heir stands in the place of the bequeather,
is
that Israel are rooted in the very Awtsmoos.
And although the matter of choice is from the aspect of the Essence, which is not compelled by anything and can desire or not desire,
nevertheless,
the matter of choice is
(not regarding the Essence itself,
but rather)
regarding His will,
that His choosing Israel is that He chose to desire them
[And there is another matter in this,
that even the choice itself
(which is the cause of the will)
is the wondrousness of the Essence
(which is not compelled by anything and can desire or not desire),
and not the Essence itself].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the name Yeshurun relates to the gift aspect from choice, while the name Yaakov relates to inheritance rooted in the Essence itself.

translations.translation: And based on this, it can be explained that regarding the matter of a gift the name Yeshurun is said, and regarding the matter of inheritance the name Yaakov,
for a gift is that it is from the aspect of the will of the giver
(as above),
coming from the choice
(that He chose to desire).
As it is said in the blessing of the Torah, “Who chose us from all the nations
(and therefore)
and gave us His Torah.”
And since the matter of choice is the wondrousness of the Essence, which is not compelled by anything,
therefore,
the vessel for this is the matter of Yeshurun, from the term “song” (shir),
a circle that has no beginning or end,
the elevation and wondrousness of the essence of the soul, which is above the division of beginning and end.
And the matter of inheritance,
that Israel are rooted in the very Awtsmoos,
is revealed in the name Yaakov,
the essential name of Israel themselves.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse “He will choose for us our inheritance, the pride of Yaakov” relates to the inheritance aspect, and on Simchas Torah the emphasis is on “Morashah Kehilas Yaakov,” expressed through dancing with the heel.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this, that in the verse “He will choose for us our inheritance” it says “the pride of Yaakov,”
is from the aspect of the matter of “our inheritance,”
for the matter of inheritance relates to Yaakov.
And the request “He will choose for us our inheritance”
is
that the matter of “our inheritance,”
the essence of the soul that is rooted in the very Awtsmoos,
should be drawn into revelation.
And just as on Rosh Hashanah the main emphasis is “our inheritance, the pride of Yaakov,” but we request that this matter be drawn into revelation,
so too is it on Simchas Torah,
that the main emphasis is “Morashah Kehilas Yaakov.”
And it says “Kehilas Yaakov,”
for from the aspect of the matter of Yaakov,
all of Israel are one existence
(a congregation),
similar to what is on Rosh Hashanah, “You are standing, etc., all of you,”
as one unit.
And this is that the commandment of the day
(of Simchas Torah)
is with dancing,
for dancing is with the legs,
and in the legs themselves—in the heel (eikev) within them
(Yaakov from the term eikev),
in which all of Israel are equal.
